crops.name: Perennial ryegrass ley
crops.overview: The backbone of Irish grassland farming. Use the Pasture Profit Index (PPI) list.
crops.ireland: Ideal — Ireland's climate is one of the best in the world for grass.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.N: Grazing: up to 250 kg N/ha/yr within Nitrates limits; silage 1st cut 100–125 kg N/ha
conventional.S: Sulphur 15–25 kg/ha on light soils/high-yield crops
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Clover provides ~100–150 kg N/ha/yr in a good sward. Spread slurry/FYM in spring; lime to pH 6.3+. Permitted rock phosphate where P index 1–2.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Grass growth in Ireland is usually limited by temperature, not water, except on light soils in dry summers.
water.critical: May–August soil moisture deficits slow growth, especially in the south-east.

harvest.timing: Graze at 1,300–1,600 kg DM/ha cover; silage mid-late May
harvest.signs: 3-leaf stage for grazing; heading for silage
harvest.storage: Silage: wilt to 25–30% DM, roll and seal well; bales wrapped 6 layers.

conventional.pests: Leatherjackets and frit fly after reseeding; rust in autumn. Herbicide for docks/thistles/chickweed at reseeding.
conventional.weeds: Post-emergence herbicide 4–6 weeks after reseeding (clover-safe products if clover sown).

organic.pests: Multispecies and clover swards, good grazing management, topping and hand-pulling docks, avoid poaching.
organic.weeds: Mowing/topping before weeds seed, dock digging, competitive sward.

crops.rotation: Leys of 3–7+ years; reseed after tillage or when sward is poor.

crops.name: White clover
crops.overview: Key to lowering fertiliser N in Irish grassland (Teagasc clover programme).

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.N: None needed — fixes 100–150 kg N/ha/yr at 20–30% sward content
conventional.S: Sulphur 15–25 kg/ha on light soils/high-yield crops
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.3–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: No fertiliser N. Keep pH 6.3–6.5, P and K index 3 (clover is sensitive to low K). Slurry in moderation.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.3–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Grass growth in Ireland is usually limited by temperature, not water, except on light soils in dry summers.
water.critical: May–August soil moisture deficits slow growth, especially in the south-east.

harvest.storage: Silage: wilt to 25–30% DM, roll and seal well; bales wrapped 6 layers.

conventional.pests: Leatherjackets and frit fly after reseeding; rust in autumn. Herbicide for docks/thistles/chickweed at reseeding.
conventional.weeds: Post-emergence herbicide 4–6 weeks after reseeding (clover-safe products if clover sown).

organic.pests: Clover-safe management: rest periods, avoid heavy N, re-sow clover by over-seeding.
organic.weeds: Mowing/topping before weeds seed, dock digging, competitive sward.

crops.rotation: Leys of 3–7+ years; reseed after tillage or when sward is poor.

crops.name: Fodder beet
crops.overview: Very high-energy winter feed; introduce to stock gradually.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.N: 120–180 kg N/ha incl. slurry; 100–150 kg Na/ha (salt); boron
conventional.S: Sulphur 15–25 kg/ha on light soils/high-yield crops
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.5–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Slurry/FYM, salt (sodium) is beneficial; boron often needed (permitted borate products if deficiency shown).
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.5–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Rain-fed; deep roots cope with dry spells.
water.critical: Canopy development June–August.

harvest.signs: Roots full size; lift before hard frost
harvest.storage: Clamp in a dry, frost-protected heap; feed by March.

conventional.pests: Aphids/virus yellows, beet cyst nematode, cercospora, powdery mildew, slugs; bolting from early sowing.
conventional.weeds: Low-dose herbicide programme (several passes) from pre-emergence.

organic.pests: Rotation, resistant varieties, sow when soil >7°C to reduce bolting, encourage beneficial insects.
organic.weeds: Very weed-sensitive: precision hoeing, finger weeders, hand-weeding; false seedbeds.

crops.rotation: 1 in 4–5 years.

crops.name: Kale (forage)
crops.overview: Hardy winter forage for cattle and sheep.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.S: Sulphur 15–25 kg/ha on light soils/high-yield crops
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Slurry/FYM before sowing; after grass ley N release is often enough.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Rain-fed. Good drainage reduces poaching at winter grazing.
water.critical: Establishment (July–Aug) on dry soils.

harvest.storage: Grazed in situ; strip-graze with a run-back area and fibre source.

conventional.pests: Flea beetle, slugs, aphids, clubroot. Winter grazing must follow Nitrates/GAEC rules (buffer zones, back-fencing).
conventional.weeds: Pre-emergence herbicide or stale seedbed.

organic.pests: Sow into moist soil for quick establishment, rotation (clubroot), resistant varieties.
organic.weeds: Stale seedbed, high seed rate, quick canopy.

crops.rotation: Not more than 1 year in 5 brassicas (clubroot).

crops.name: Forage/grazing rye
crops.overview: Early spring grazing from an autumn sowing.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.S: Sulphur 15–25 kg/ha on light soils/high-yield crops
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: N from clover/grass ley or legume preceding crop, cattle FYM or composted manure (≤170 kg organic N/ha/yr whole farm), slurry in spring. P/K from manures; permitted rock phosphate and permitted potassium sulphate (natural origin) if soil test low. Lime to pH 6.5.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Irish rainfall (750–1,200 mm) normally meets needs; irrigation not used. Avoid waterlogging over winter.
water.critical: Stem extension to grain fill (May–July) is when drought hurts yield, mainly on light soils.

harvest.storage: Dry to 14–15% moisture (malting 12–13%), cool and aerate; check for insects.

conventional.pests: Aphids/BYDV (autumn insecticide or BYDV-tolerant variety), slugs after OSR/grass, Septoria, rusts, mildew, Ramularia/net blotch (barley), take-all in second cereals. Use a T0–T3 fungicide plan based on variety ratings and Teagasc/DAFM advice.
conventional.weeds: Pre-/early post-emergence herbicide in autumn, follow-up in spring for cleavers, wild oats, brome, blackgrass where present.

organic.pests: Choose varieties with high disease ratings (DAFM Recommended List); later sowing to cut BYDV risk; wider rotations (no second cereal) against take-all; variety mixtures; undersown clover. No synthetic fungicides or insecticides.
organic.weeds: Stale seedbed, delayed sowing, higher seed rate, comb-harrowing/tine weeding at 3–5 leaves, competitive tall varieties.

crops.rotation: Avoid second and third cereals (take-all, grass weeds). Good after grass, beans, OSR or potatoes.

crops.name: Westerwolds ryegrass
crops.overview: Annual ryegrass for a quick bulk of silage or grazing.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.S: Sulphur 15–25 kg/ha on light soils/high-yield crops
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Clover provides ~100–150 kg N/ha/yr in a good sward. Spread slurry/FYM in spring; lime to pH 6.3+. Permitted rock phosphate where P index 1–2.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Grass growth in Ireland is usually limited by temperature, not water, except on light soils in dry summers.
water.critical: May–August soil moisture deficits slow growth, especially in the south-east.

harvest.storage: Silage: wilt to 25–30% DM, roll and seal well; bales wrapped 6 layers.

conventional.pests: Leatherjackets and frit fly after reseeding; rust in autumn. Herbicide for docks/thistles/chickweed at reseeding.
conventional.weeds: Post-emergence herbicide 4–6 weeks after reseeding (clover-safe products if clover sown).

organic.pests: Multispecies and clover swards, good grazing management, topping and hand-pulling docks, avoid poaching.
organic.weeds: Mowing/topping before weeds seed, dock digging, competitive sward.

crops.rotation: Leys of 3–7+ years; reseed after tillage or when sward is poor.

crops.name: Peas/barley arable silage mix
crops.overview: High-protein wholecrop silage.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.S: Sulphur 15–25 kg/ha on light soils/high-yield crops
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: No N needed (fixes its own). P/K from FYM or permitted rock phosphate/potassium sulphate if index 1.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Rain-fed; beans tolerate heavier land, peas need free drainage.
water.critical: Flowering and pod set (June–July).

harvest.storage: Dry to 14% (beans) and keep cool.

conventional.pests: Bean weevil, black bean aphid, chocolate spot, downy mildew (beans); pea moth, pea aphid (peas).
conventional.weeds: Pre-emergence herbicide; limited post-emergence options.

organic.pests: Resistant/tolerant varieties, later sowing of spring beans to avoid weevil peak, encourage ladybirds and hoverflies (field margins).
organic.weeds: Blind harrowing before emergence, inter-row hoeing; good seedbed.

crops.rotation: 1 in 5 years (foot rots, sclerotinia). Leaves N for the next cereal.
